summary: Argentina is in a quieter stretch under President Milei. Monthly inflation was 1.9% in September, in line with the central bank's survey of economists and up from 1.7% in August, and yearly inflation is 33.4%. Prices are up 23.6% so far in 2026. Reserves were about $48.7 billion on Oct 5 and the central bank has been buying dollars. The IMF's third program review is still open after a Sep 21 to 29 mission. Argentine stocks move on inflation prints, reserves and the IMF, and energy names also ride Vaca Muerta shale output and oil prices. On Oct 22 country risk topped 700 (709), the official dollar hit a nominal record of 1,550 pesos and the Merval fell 1.5% to 97,993.
for_you: Argentina is a high risk, high swing market. YPF and VIST ride oil above $100. Keep any trade small, and check the inflation print on Oct 13 first.

summary: Brazil voted on Oct 4 and the result surprised markets. Flavio Bolsonaro took about 47% of valid votes to Lula's about 45%, so the two meet in a runoff on Oct 25. Investors read his lead as a sign of spending cuts and reform, and Brazilian stocks and the real jumped: the Ibovespa rose 7.7% on Oct 5 and hit a new record of 209,067 on Oct 9, with the real near 5.00 per dollar. The central bank cut the Selic to 13.75% on Sep 16, but September inflation came in at 4.58% over 12 months, above the 4.5% ceiling, which limits more cuts. The rally has priced in a Bolsonaro win (prediction markets near 87% to 89% on Oct 10), so a Lula comeback on Oct 25 is the main risk, and a 25% US Section 301 tariff on many Brazilian goods (since Jul 22) still hangs over exporters and the Pix payment system. The runoff has tightened: Quaest (Oct 14) and Datafolha (Oct 15, per O Povo) both show 51% to 49% for Flavio Bolsonaro, inside the margin of error. A Vox Brasil poll taken Oct 15 to 17 is the first recent poll with Lula ahead, 51% to 49% of valid votes. New polls on Oct 20 mostly lean to Bolsonaro: Real Time Big Data has 52% to 48% and Gerp 53% to 47%, while Data Ranking has Lula 50.4% to 49.6%. The Ibovespa rose 1.57% to 208,295.98 on Oct 20 and the real firmed to about 5.02. Quaest's Oct 21 poll has Flavio Bolsonaro at 45% and Lula at 44%, down from 46% to 44% a week earlier, so the race is within one point. The final polls before Sunday's runoff show a tie: Datafolha 50% to 50% of valid votes and PoderData 51% to 49% for Flavio Bolsonaro, both released Oct 22.
for_you: The Oct 25 runoff is close to a coin flip. NU is 'Buy zone now' (14.56 on Oct 16, zone 14.03 to 15.08), but wait until after the vote before buying or selling puts on Brazil names: a Lula win could knock Brazilian banks 5% to 10% in a day. The BBD insider cluster (22 insiders, about $100 million, last buys Sep 28) still stands. MELI is rated Avoid.

summary: The US and China extended their October 2025 trade truce in late September 2026, and China delayed its rare earth export ban to Jan 10. Tariffs are still high: about 36.5% on Chinese goods into the US and 31% on US goods into China, per a July 2026 Congressional Research Service report. On Oct 9 China and the EU reached an interim understanding to roughly halve Chinese hybrid car exports to the EU over four years, and China will cut duties on about EUR 4 billion of EU goods; EU leaders still have to approve it. China is also pushing into memory chips: CXMT's fifth generation DRAM platform is in mass production and its world share passed 10%, which hit Micron and Korean chipmakers on Oct 12. Chinese large caps are weak, with the Shanghai 50 at a 14 month low. September exports rose 36.3% from a year ago and the monthly surplus hit $133.5 billion (Oct 14), with chip exports up 108.1%. Q3 GDP grew 4.5% (Oct 19), just above forecasts, but shoppers stayed weak and investment fell, so big new stimulus looks less likely. On Oct 22 the CSI 300 closed 20.2% below its June 22 peak, its first bear market since 2020, after 10 straight weekly losses, as AI stocks slid across Asia.
for_you: China matters to you mostly through US names that sell there and through memory supply. AAPL is 'Accumulate on pullback', QCOM is 'Wait' and NVDA is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' on Oct 15 data. A record trade surplus raises the odds of a new tariff fight before the Jan 10 rare earth deadline, and rising Chinese chip exports back the CXMT worry for MU. Size swings normally and skip memory.

summary: Europe is fighting an energy shock from the Iran war. Euro area inflation was 3.2% in August, with energy up 14.3% from a year ago, and markets expect the ECB to keep raising rates from a deposit rate of about 2.50% (next decision Oct 29). The brief Russia Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' has failed: Zelenskyy said Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian refineries, and Russia reported a hit on the Ryazan refinery on Oct 15, which keeps diesel tight into winter. ASML beat and raised on Oct 14. High energy hurts chemicals and industry, while oil majors and banks gain. Reuters reported on Oct 17 that the Ryazan refinery's main crude unit is still halted after the Oct 15 strike, and a drone set fire to Russia's Surgut condensate plant on Oct 16. On Oct 19 riots in France pushed its 10 year yield toward 4.9% and hit French banks, with a Moody's review due Oct 23. The US waived new Russia oil tariffs on Oct 16, easing oil but angering Kyiv. France did not vote on its budget on Oct 20: the National Assembly set the revenue vote for Nov 3, so Moody's (Aa3, negative outlook) reviews France on Oct 23 with no budget decision. The prime minister promised more curfews, and the CAC 40 fell 0.38% to 7,838.49 on Oct 20. On Oct 21 France's 10 year yield touched 5%, its highest since 2002, and it reached about 5.10% on Oct 22, with the gap over Germany near its widest since 2011, a day before Moody's review.
for_you: Europe is fighting energy driven inflation and now French fiscal stress. More ECB hikes are likely (Oct 29). European bank ADRs (SAN, ING) gain from higher rates but are hurt by the French selloff, so wait until after Moody's on Oct 23. ASML is the one European name that matters for your AI themes.

summary: The US-Iran war that began Feb 28, 2026 has left the Strait of Hormuz mostly shut to commercial ships for over seven months. The war is now inside Saudi Arabia: Houthi strikes on Riyadh's airport killed at least 13 on Oct 10, and on Oct 14 a ballistic missile hit an Aramco office building at its Dhahran headquarters, damaging the floors used by top executives. Ships keep getting hit: UKMTO reported a tanker and two container ships struck near Hormuz on Oct 13. Brent was about $106.30 on the morning of Oct 14. A Houthi official said Russia and China have reached out about a ceasefire. Qatar shipped only 18 LNG cargoes in the war's first six months against 509 a year earlier. Most Gulf champions like Aramco are not US listed, so the US trade is through oil producers, US LNG exporters, oil service firms and the KSA ETF. On Oct 16 Brent settled at $109.86, its highest since May 19, after a record pace of ship attacks near Hormuz, and on Oct 17 a missile aimed at Yanbu, the Saudi port that bypasses Hormuz, was shot down. On Oct 17 Iran said its seven day plan to reopen Hormuz still stands if the US lifts its blockade and oil sanctions, and the Revolutionary Guards claimed a second supertanker hit a mine (not independently confirmed). On Oct 19 Brent touched $106.82 after the US waived new Russia tariffs, then settled at $109.55, down only 0.3%, and traded above $110 early Oct 20 after the Houthis claimed new strikes on Saudi sites at Yanbu and Shaybah (not confirmed by Saudi authorities). US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Gulf oil flows are back to about 80% of prewar levels, a US government figure, and that some sanctioned dark fleet tankers will be allowed to carry legal crude; Kpler thinks only about 24 qualify. On Oct 20 Iran's Revolutionary Guards said mines stopped three tankers near Hormuz; CENTCOM called the claims false and said the waterways are cleared of mines. Brent touched $111.99, then settled down 0.69% at $108.79 as Pakistan's army chief took a mediation plan to Tehran. Kpler counts at least 18 ships attacked in two weeks. On Oct 21 to 22 a drone strike on Aramco's Shaybah field killed two people without affecting operations, an attack on Dammam's airport killed one, and the US ordered some embassy staff to leave Saudi Arabia; Brent rose as much as 3.3% to $112.43. Brent settled at $113.17 on Oct 22, up about 4% and its highest close since May 4, even though Kpler showed Hormuz flows near prewar levels: the market is pricing the next strike, not lost barrels.
for_you: This is the biggest outside risk to your whole dashboard. Oil above $100 because of Hormuz feeds US inflation, Fed hikes and market swings. Helped: CVX and LNG exporters. If you hold swings, a big Gulf headline is the most likely reason for a sudden gap down, so always have stops set.

summary: India's central bank raised its repo rate 0.25 point to 5.50% on Oct 7, its first hike since February 2023, and said a cut is off the table for now. Inflation is forecast at 5.2% this fiscal year, pushed up by oil above $100, which India mostly imports. On Oct 12 the rupee rebounded about 1% to near 95.7 to 95.8 per dollar after RBI steps to curb dollar demand in the spot market, but stocks fell for another day as bond yields rose for a fourth session and foreign outflows reached about Rs 3 lakh crore; the Sensex was near 71,900 midday. The February trade deal with the US has stalled, and a 10% US Section 301 tariff has applied to most Indian goods since Jul 24. A weak rupee helps IT exporters like Infosys; higher rates and oil weigh on banks and consumers. September consumer inflation rose to 5.54% (Oct 12), above the RBI's 5.2% forecast. On Oct 16 the US waived new tariffs on buyers of Russian oil, removing a threat to India, and oil eased about 2% on Oct 19.
for_you: India just raised rates and the rupee is weak. That helps outsourcers (INFY, WIT) and hurts banks and travel. Nothing here is on your lists; low priority.

The yen firmed to just under 158 per dollar as investors sought safety. A weak yen helps exporters like Toyota and Sony, and higher rates help the big banks. The Nikkei fell 1.30% to 64,075.42 on Oct 20 as SoftBank and chip suppliers sold off, then rose 0.85% to 64,621.24 on Oct 21 after Super Micro and SpaceX results, with Advantest up about 5.3%.

The trigger was Banxico's Oct 8 minutes, which left the door open to rate cuts from 6.50% and said Mexico need not follow the Fed, so the carry trade that held the peso up is weakening. The USMCA was not renewed in July and moved to annual reviews, so trade rules for cars and factories stay uncertain. A weaker peso cuts the dollar value of Mexican companies' profits but lowers costs for companies that make goods in Mexico and sell in the US.
for_you: A weaker peso and rate cuts help the airport stocks (ASR, PAC) more than consumer names. Nothing here is a setup today. Watch only if you want Mexico exposure.

summary: Korean stocks are in a bear market. The KOSPI fell 7.57% to 5,554.22 on Oct 15, its seventh straight loss and lowest close since April 7, tripping a sidecar and a Level 1 circuit breaker; Korea Times puts it about 40% below its June 19 peak of 9,385. SK hynix fell about 11% and Samsung about 9.5% on doubts about AI returns, a possible memory glut from China's CXMT, and the chance of another US rate hike. Server DRAM spot prices are still rising, so the stocks are falling faster than the business. The Bank of Korea raised its rate to 3.0% in August and meets Oct 22; SK hynix reports Oct 28 and Samsung Oct 29. Samsung and SK hynix have no regular US listing, so US investors reach Korea mostly through EWY, Korean bank ADRs and Coupang. On Oct 16 the index bounced: about 2.1% to 5,668.05 early (AP) and about 4.1% to 5,782.62 in a later Saxo update; the close was not confirmed at writing. The Oct 16 close was 5,668.06, up 2.05%, but the KOSPI lost 14.46% for the week, its worst week since October 2008. Surveys published Oct 18 expect the Bank of Korea to hold at 3.00% on Oct 22 and hike in November. On Oct 20 the KOSPI fell 3.73% to 5,552.74, its lowest close since April 7, then rose 3.29% to 5,735.66 on Oct 21 as foreigners bought a net 660 billion won and the won firmed to 1,325.2 per dollar, its strongest since October 2024. The Bank of Korea decides at 10am Seoul time Oct 22 (9pm ET Oct 21); a hold at 3.00% is expected. On Oct 22 the Bank of Korea held at 3.00% in a unanimous vote but said more hikes depend on Q3 GDP and inflation, and the KOSPI fell 3.52% to 5,533.77, its lowest close since April. On Oct 23 the KOSPI recovered from an early 2.36% drop to close up 0.30% at 5,550.30 as SK hynix rose about 4.4% after halting a Nasdaq listing review for its Solidigm unit; foreigners still sold a net 994.1 billion won. SK hynix reports before 9am Seoul time on Oct 28 (8pm ET Oct 27).
for_you: Korea is a memory chip market, and AI doubts hit it first. Skip MU and memory swings until the selling stops. Korean bank ADRs (KB, SHG) are mixed: a hawkish hold helps their margins but the market selloff hurts. No new buys before SK hynix reports Oct 28.

summary: Taiwan's story is the AI chip boom. On Oct 15 TSMC reported Q3 revenue of $46.72 billion, up 41.2%, a 66.4% gross margin, a Q4 guide of $52.3 to $54.3 billion, and raised 2026 growth to about 44%, saying AI demand is far above supply. Its shares still fell about 2% and the Taiex had its sixth biggest point drop ever, with record net foreign selling of NT$302.56 billion, as global investors cut AI exposure on rate and debt fears. The main local risks remain China-Taiwan tension or US chip tariffs; no new tension was found this week. The Taiex fell 1.13% on Oct 20, then rose 1.28% to 46,887.77 on Oct 21, led by AI server and chip names after Super Micro raised its sales outlook. The Taiex fell 1.81% to 46,041.43 on Oct 22 as US chip stocks crashed, and Taipei was closed on Oct 23 for Typhoon Champi, so Taiwan has not yet traded the second day of the AI sell off.
for_you: Taiwan is the AI factory. TSMC sales are still growing over 50% a year, which supports NVDA, AMD and the whole AI compute theme. TSMC reports Thursday Oct 15: avoid opening new AI chip swings before that call, and use any post earnings dip in NVDA (Buy zone now) as a long term entry.
